cards.text: Friend, Proverbs hands the mic to a new voice: Agur son of Jakeh, and these are his words, the burden he declared to Ithiel. He opens with, 'I am weary, O God, and worn out.' No hello, no good morning, just TIRED, and honestly, same.
Then Agur sizes himself up: 'Surely I am the most ignorant of men, and I lack the understanding of a man.' Friend, that is the humblest résumé I have EVER read.

cards.question: True or false: Agur says he has learned wisdom and has knowledge of the Holy One.

cards.text: Then Agur fires off some HUGE questions: 'Who has ascended to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in His hands?'

cards.question: Agur keeps going: who has bound up the waters in His cloak and established all the ends of the earth? Who could do all of that?

cards.text: Then Agur asks what His name is, and what the name of His Son is, and finishes with 'surely you know!' For a man who says he lacks understanding, Agur asks REALLY good questions.

cards.question: After those huge questions, Agur names something that is flawless. What is it?
True or false: Agur says God is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
Since every word of God is flawless, what does Agur warn against?

cards.text: Agur says not to add to His words, lest He rebuke you and prove you a liar. Flawless doesn't need upgrades, friend, and I say that as a stamper who once 'upgraded' a perfect recipe with TRIPLE sprinkles.
Now Agur talks to God. He says he's asking for two things, and adds, 'do not refuse me before I die.'

cards.question: Agur just said every word of God is flawless. What's the first thing he asks God for?

answers.text: To keep lies far from him
To give him a long life

cards.question: True or false: for his second request, Agur asks God to make him rich.

cards.text: Agur asks for neither poverty nor riches, just 'the bread that is my portion.' Not the whole bakery, just his share, and as a guy who OWNS a whole bakery, I'm sitting with that one.

cards.question: Why doesn't Agur want riches?
And if Agur becomes poor, he says he might ___ and profane the name of his God.

cards.text: Agur's prayer is done. Now he turns to how people treat each other, starting with what you say about a servant to his master.

cards.question: True or false: Agur says if you slander a servant to his master, you'll be cursed and you'll bear the guilt.

cards.text: Then Agur starts a list, and every line opens the same way: 'There is a generation.'

cards.question: Agur's first generation curses their ___ and does not bless their mothers.
True or false: Agur says the generation that's pure in their own eyes really is clean.

cards.text: The next generation has haughty eyes and pretentious glances. You know that look: the guy in the fancy car when you pull up next to him with a missing hubcap.

cards.question: Agur says the last generation's teeth are swords and their jaws are knives. Who do they devour?

cards.text: Then Agur says, 'The leech has two daughters: Give and Give.' Friend, that's every subscription I forgot to cancel.

cards.question: True or false: Agur lists Sheol, the barren womb, land that never has enough water, and fire as things that are never satisfied.

cards.text: Then Agur circles back to the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother.

cards.question: What does Agur say about the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother?

answers.text: May the ravens pluck it out
May the lions of the field tear it
May the jackals of the desert eat it

cards.text: Ravens AND vultures, friend. Agur does NOT play about Mom and Dad. Next, the man who said he lacks understanding lists four things he cannot understand.

cards.question: Agur can't understand the way of an eagle in the sky, a snake on a rock, a ship at sea, or a man with a maiden. How does he describe these four things?

cards.text: Then Agur describes the way of an adulteress: she eats and wipes her mouth.

cards.question: The adulteress eats and wipes her mouth. What does she say afterward?

answers.text: I am sorry for what I did

cards.text: Agur's got more threes and fours for us. Under three things, he says, the earth trembles, and under four it cannot bear up.
First on the list: a servant who becomes king, and a fool who is filled with food. That second one is me after I 'taste-test' an ENTIRE batch.

cards.question: Agur's list also has an unloved woman who marries. What's the last thing the earth can't bear up under?

answers.text: A maidservant who takes her mistress's place
A mistress who serves her own maidservant
A son who takes his father's land

cards.text: Then Agur flips it: 'Four things on earth are small, yet they are exceedingly wise.' FINALLY, a list for little guys like me.

cards.question: First on the small but wise list: the ants. They're creatures of little strength, so what do they do that's wise?

answers.text: Store up their food in summer

cards.text: Next, the rock badgers. Agur says they're creatures of little power, and friend, I RELATE.

cards.question: The rock badgers don't have much power. So where do they make their homes?
True or false: the locusts have no king, so they scatter in every direction.
Agur says the lizard can be caught in one's hands. But where is it found?

cards.text: A lizard in the PALACE, and I spent YEARS in a junk drawer. Then Agur's last list: three things stately in their stride, four impressive in their walk.

cards.question: True or false: Agur says the lion, mighty among beasts, retreats when danger comes.
Agur names a lion, a strutting rooster, a he-goat, and a ___ with his army around him.
Agur says if you've foolishly exalted yourself or plotted evil, what should you do?

answers.text: Put your hand over your mouth

cards.text: Then Agur gives the reason with pictures: churning milk yields butter, and twisting the nose draws blood.

cards.question: Agur says churning milk yields butter and twisting the nose draws blood, so the stirring of anger brings forth ___.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "A mistress who serves her own maidservant" describes the same role reversal as the right answer "A maidservant who takes her mistress's place." If the maidservant supplants her mistress, the mistress ends up under her, so a baker could argue this wrong answer is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "In the king's armory" is very close to the right answer "In the palaces of kings." Both are royal buildings, and a king's armory could sit inside his palace, so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "peace" and "wisdom" don't work after "the stirring of anger brings forth ___." The setup about twisting the nose until it bleeds makes "peace" an obvious opposite, close to silly. Neither wrong answer is believable.

rule.text: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The right answer "May the ravens pluck it out" leaves out the verse's place phrase ("of the valley"). Both wrong answers include one ("of the field," "of the desert"). That makes the right answer shorter and different in shape, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The question asks where the rock badgers make their homes, and the right answer is "In the rocks." The creature's name, which appears in the question and on story card 6, already gives the answer away. This doesn't come from an earlier card's wording but from the BSB name itself.
findings.question: When the answer to a choice card is contained in a name the text uses, like "rock badgers" and "in the rocks," does that count as giving the answer away? Should the card instead ask about what makes the badgers wise (weak, yet living in a strong place)?

findings.problem: Proverbs 30:19 (the eagle, the snake, the ship, and the man with a maiden) is told only inside this choice card's question. The card cites only Proverbs 30:18, the verse of its right answer, so no card in the walkthrough cites 30:19.
findings.question: Must every verse of the passage be cited by at least one card? Or is it fine for a verse to be covered only inside a choice card's question, where the citation rule allows only the right answer's verse?
